headline: Google and HKU report platform-agnostic verification for computer-use agents
summary: A distinct Oct 29 arXiv paper by Google and The University of Hong Kong authors, arXiv:2610.40578, introduces a platform-agnostic framework named VeriCUA. An earlier Oct 19 paper from a different author group uses the same acronym for a learned GUI reward verifier; the two papers are separate. The later framework gathers evidence through GUI and code checks, links findings to observed sources, and can abstain when evidence does not settle a requirement. Across five reported benchmark settings, the authors find higher agreement with reference labels than selected verifier baselines. The results are author-reported and limited to the studied environments and model setup; offline unresolved cases may fall back to an initial VLM judgment, and the paper reports substantially higher token and call costs than single-call judging.
